Renewable Thermal Collaborative (2023). Renewable Thermal Vision Report: Industrial Thermal Decarbonization Package (executive presentation, appendices, six sector perspectives and eight technology perspectives), analysis by Boston Consulting Group; updated September 2023. https://www.renewablethermal.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Decarbonization_FullPackage_Updated-Sept-2023.pdf

A 200-slide consulting deck: almost every number is a chart without printed values. Locators are slide numbers, which equal PDF page numbers. Main file: printed maximum temperatures by technology (p.11-12), the efficiencies behind the LCOH and fuel-cost comparisons (p.12, pp.136-146), the two heat pump case studies (p.135) and the printed LCOH values on the thermal-storage slide (p.182). Sidecars (not loaded): _ccs-cost-increase (p.114, cost increase per tonne of ammonia, steel, clinker, glass and methanol with thermal-only vs full-facility CCS); _process-temperatures (iron and steel p.75, chemicals p.55, pulp and paper p.88); _other-values. Not extracted: the LCOH bar charts (p.12-13 and sector slides) and projected LCOH lines, the solar thermal capex curve (p.172), RNG and biomass supply cost curves (pp.159-161, 194-195), state maps and emissions charts.

(1) p.11 places the Electromagnetic 2,000 degC label inside the Bioethanol bar. (2) Efficiency assumptions differ between slides: natural gas combustion 75% (LCOH, p.12) vs 85% (fuel cost, pp.136-146); electric resistance 99% (p.12) vs 100% (p.146). (3) The title is printed as Industrial Thermal Decarbonization Package; the web file is named Renewable Thermal Vision Report.
